Revision semantics proven by real mutation: changed document (revision changes, stale SENSITIVE-USER-TEXT absent), emptied requests (revision changes again, deleted request gone), truncated journal operation (exit 1 with EMPTY stdout - no prefix publication), completed late append (new revision, late record present), and seeded SQLite late/update/delete where delete leaves exactly one record, the closing manifest alone - the contract's observable-empty-projection clause end to end.

Checkpoint-after-output proven with a real failing writer: the consumer's PartialThenFail accepts 11 bytes then returns BrokenPipe; the probe asserts PipelineErrorKind::Write, exactly 11 bytes landed and no checkpoint, then retries successfully, publishing checkpoint_on_failure false and partial_bytes 11 - an honest statement that bytes can land while no checkpoint issues. A deleted source likewise yields exit 1 and empty stdout.

Filesystem storage safety read line by line: O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK with a non-regular-file rejection closes the leaf-symlink race and FIFO stall; verify re-checks symlink_metadata and the live descriptor against dev/ino plus a (len, mtime, mtime_nsec, ctime, ctime_nsec) stamp for JSON; the in-file test walks append, truncate, rewrite-with-restored-mtime, rename-replace, unlink and symlink-swap, deliberately restoring mtime to prove ctime carries detection. SQLite skips the stamp with a stated WAL reason while keeping dev/ino.

SQLite path is the strongest component: canonicalises only the trusted parent and rejoins the filename so SQLITE_OPEN_NOFOLLOW still guards the leaf; read-only, no URI, explicit rejection of immutable=1 because it would discard live WAL updates; trusted schema and views disabled; SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH bounded; non-UTF-8 database encodings refused rather than under-budgeted; pragma_table_list and table_xinfo verify an ordinary table with real non-hidden key/value columns, excluding views, virtual and generated columns; octet_length preflight on stored columns with ORDER BY deliberately omitted to avoid an unbounded sorter, sorting in Rust so the revision stays deterministic; duplicate keys rejected. Table name is constrained to [A-Za-z0-9_] by validate and quoted.

Revision digest is collision-resistant by construction: domain-separated with 'unisphere.snapshot.v1\0', includes format and table, and length-prefixes every key and value, so two different key/value partitions cannot collide into one revision.

Mapper purity is structural, not promised: every adapter crate is #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and the architecture sensor restricts adapter dependencies to unisphere-core, serde_json and time, admitting rusqlite only for loader-snapshot and as an app dev-dependency, so a mapper cannot acquire a database handle.

Keys are native or documented-structural throughout: 'document', loader 'journal:<ordinal>', exact cursorDiskKV strings, and JSON-Pointer-style suffixes such as 'document#/requests/0/message'. The reduced VS Code journal is keyed 'journal:reduced' rather than attributed to any single physical line, and the manifest's '$snapshot' sentinel is clearly synthetic rather than a pretend native key.

findings.description: The VS Code journal reducer bounds synthesized sparse-array nulls at total_raw_bytes/4, which correctly stops a tiny hostile 'i' from requesting gigabytes, but the budget counts serde_json::Value slots while the comment reasons in JSON bytes. Each slot costs size_of::<Value>() resident bytes, not four, so a single crafted operation inside a 32 MiB record can claim roughly 8M null slots and peak memory becomes a multiple of max_snapshot_bytes rather than comparable to it. Bounded and non-fatal, and the direction is right, but an operator sizing a collector from max_snapshot_bytes will under-predict RSS. Accepted rather than held because the failure mode is memory pressure under a hostile local file, not incorrect output or an unbounded allocation. My multiplier is arithmetic, not measurement: PM should measure before choosing between bounding holes against max_records and documenting the ratio in docs/snapshot-loader.md.
findings.evidence: crates/adapter-vscode-copilot/src/journal.rs reduce() computes holes as the checked sum of record byte lengths divided by 4, and extend() decrements that budget by the number of added elements before array.resize(length, Value::Null), erroring with BatchLimit on exhaustion; crates/core/src/snapshot.rs SnapshotLimits::default() is max_record_bytes 32 MiB and max_snapshot_bytes 64 MiB.

findings.description: vscode-copilot's descriptor advertises four location hints, two with storage_format json_document and two with json_journal, while its registry entry pins SourceRepresentation::JsonDocument. Exporting a real *.jsonl journal therefore requires the operator to add --source-format json-journal; without it the journal is parsed as a single document and fails InvalidData. It fails closed and never mismaps, and proof/native.rs covers the journal path explicitly, so this is a discoverability cliff rather than a correctness hole. It is also nearly free to close because the machine-readable answer is already published in the catalog: the CLI could derive the format from the matched hint's storage_format instead of requiring the operator to restate it.
